summary: Scope: Root decision on FS-GG/.github#4778 (comment 6390313337, 2026-10-24T22:26Z), not a provisioned image. The first candidate carrier Ubuntu 26.10 ships openssl 4.0.3 (official cloud package manifest read 2026-10-24), but eng/bar_hosted_operation.py crypto_identity requires the installed OpenSSL family to start with 'OpenSSL 3.' before sealing the encrypted BAR candidate. The reviewed layer's verify-guest reported openssl-family-not-3 and the bake refused to finish, which surfaced the mismatch before any dispatch. Root chose the Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (noble) cloud image (openssl 3.0.x), signature-verified and pinned by hash, rather than relaxing the gate or qualifying OpenSSL 4; the gate and its readback stay unchanged so a later OpenSSL 4 carrier is refused again. Consequences: noble's glibc is 2.39 whereas FS.GG.SDD CatalogScaffoldLinux.fs accepts exactly 2.44, so this carrier cannot serve catalog-dependent callers (Templates callers stay unrouted); acquired-input-lock.json, package-inventory.expected and an APT transaction were regenerated for noble's package set including runner dependencies (libicu74, libkrb5-3, zlib1g) by the delivery that carries this record (Coordination #1069; cite its merged files for the lock itself); the actions/runner tarball has no bin/runnerversion file (version is read from bin/Runner.Listener.deps.json). Lesson: an executable readback of a carrier against existing source gates finds incompatibilities earlier than reading release notes.
title: Dedicated runner carrier is Ubuntu 24.04 noble because the BAR CMS gate accepts only OpenSSL 3
